To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the behavioral aggravations of the IDPN induced dyskinesia by the CsA administration may result from the acceleration of the presynaptic and postsynaptic dopaminergic systems via the activation of transcription factors, which bind upstream to the tyrosine hydroxyase and D1 receptor genes.

the behavioral aggravations of the IDPN induced dyskinesia may be due to activation of transcription factors, and that immunophilin binding agent, such as CsA, may be involved in the aggravated dyskinesias.

the behavioral aggravations of dyskinesias induced by IDPN are associated with the increase of dopamine levels, the increase of transcription factors binding to TRE and CRE in the striatum, and the decrease of D1-receptors mRNA levels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the involvement of the immunophilin ligand in the pathogenesis of the IDPN model of tardive dyskinesia.
the involvement of immunosuppressive agents in the pathogenesis of dyskinesias.
the effects of CsA administration on IDPN-induced dyskinetic behavior, and the changes in the levels of dopamine and the activities of TRE- and CRE-binding proteins in rat brain.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effects of the immunophilin ligand on the pathogenesis and/or pathophysiology of the IDPN model of dyskinesias are complex and not well understood.
immunophilins and the immunophilin ligand, CsA, are involved in the pathogenesis of dyskinesias.

immunophilin ligand binding agents are involved in the pathophysiology of the IDPN model and that the IDPN-induced behavioral abnormality is a good model for the study of the pathogenesis of dyskinesias in humans.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the activation of the immunophilins by immunophilin ligand, such as CsA, may be involved in the pathogenesis of dyskinesias.

the immunophilins are involved in the pathophysiology of neurotoxicity and neurodegenerative diseases, and that they are potential targets for the development of novel therapeutics for neurotoxicity, dyskinesia or neurodegenerative disorders.
the immunophilins, FK506 binding proteins, and cyclophilins may have an important role in the regulation of the dopaminegic system and in the pathogenesis of dyskinesias induced by neuroleptics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use the immunophilin ligand to modulate the transcriptional regulation of tyrosine hydroxylation and dopamine receptor genes, thereby modulating the dopaminegic neurotransmission in the brain.
immunophilin binding ligands are involved in the pathogenesis of dyskinesias.
the immunophilins are a novel class of drug targets for the treatment of neurodegenerative disorders.
